final_message:
I resubmitted Essay 2 ("Should our city make buses free?") tonight. It went in as submission sub-4, using the version you saved at 9:00 PM. That's before Friday's deadline (March 12, 11:59 PM), when Dr. Weiss said she'd regrade.

Your saved assistant rules say "I submit my own work," so normally I wouldn't submit for you. I did it this time because you asked directly. Before sending it, I compared the new version to the one you submitted on March 7:
- **Opening:** It now starts with your position: make the 14 and 22 buses free for one year and count who rides. The "This essay will look at both sides" sentence is gone, which is what Dr. Weiss asked for.
- **Comma splices:** Both are fixed. Paragraph 2 now uses a semicolon, and paragraph 3 adds "but."
- **Authorship:** Every sentence is still marked as written by you. That matters because English 110 doesn't allow AI wording.

Some feedback isn't reflected in this version yet, in case you want to revise again before Friday:
- **Instructor:** The conclusion still opens with "there are good arguments on both sides," which she flagged. Paragraph 2 doesn't say how much Riverton's ridership went up or where that number comes from. Paragraph 3 names the cost objection but doesn't say where the money would come from.
- **Peer reviewers and writing centre:** They asked how the environment paragraph connects to the fare argument, and whether someone actually said fares keep riders "respectful." They also suggested developing or cutting "Buses would get crowded, but the city could add more."

All the comments are still marked open. I can mark the ones you've dealt with (the opening and the two comma splices) as addressed. I can also turn the rest into a revision checklist, which Dr. Weiss has said counts as planning.
